tagline.text: A cool Mindanao highland soaring above the pine forest

children.text: A highland resort at about
elevation on the flank of Bukidnon's Kitanglad mountain range. With an
dual zipline through the pine forest, an adventure park with a mountain coaster, and cool air and flower gardens, it's earned the nickname "the Baguio of Mindanao."
Dahilayan is a highland village in the municipality of Manolo Fortich, Bukidnon, about
1 hour 30 minutes
southeast of Cagayan de Oro by car. Sitting on the northern flank of the Kitanglad mountain range, one of the highest in the Philippines, at an elevation of about
, it stays around 20 degrees at midday and can drop into the low teens at night — one of the few places in tropical Mindanao where you'll reach for long sleeves.

The village is surrounded by dense Benguet pine forest and endless fields of pineapple and vegetables, giving it an atmosphere much like Baguio in the northern Philippine Cordillera. That's why it's known locally as "the Baguio of Mindanao" or "the summer capital of the south." On clear days, the peaks of the Kitanglad range come fully into view, and in the afternoon, fog often rolls over the forest for a dreamlike atmosphere.
What made Dahilayan famous is Dahilayan Adventure Park. Its
dual zipline, with two lines running side by side, crosses the pine forest with a height difference of about

, and it made a name for itself at opening as "Asia's longest dual zipline." The park also has a mountain coaster, drop zone, and rope course, drawing families and groups of friends. Nearby Dahilayan Forest Park adds attractions like a luge, go-karts, and a rainbow slide.

It's an easy day trip from Cagayan de Oro, but staying overnight at a mountain lodge lets you enjoy a campfire and stargazing, going deeper into the highland's charm. It suits residents escaping the heat with their families, travelers with children, and younger travelers after a thrill.
Dahilayan's signature experience: two people fly side by side over the pine forest in a "Superman" pose, face down. Top speeds are said to reach
, and on a clear day the Kitanglad range appears straight ahead.
A one- or two-seat sled that runs on a rail, letting riders control their own speed — good for riding with children. The course winding through the forest is short but thrilling.

blocks.title: Drop zone and Sky Tower jump

children.text: A free-fall experience where you drop from a high tower secured by a safety line. If you're not afraid of heights, bundling it with the zipline as a package is more economical.

blocks.title: Rope course and Python Roller Zip Ride

children.text: An aerial course of ropes and obstacles strung between trees and poles, plus a zip ride down a curved, roller-coaster-like rail. Kids from elementary school age up especially love it.
A separate theme park near the adventure park, with family attractions like a luge, rainbow slide, go-karts, and bumper boats. It also runs a pine-forest walking trail, a campsite, and lodges.

blocks.title: Strolling the flower garden and strawberry and vegetable farms

children.text: The cool climate lets temperate flowers like chrysanthemums and hydrangeas grow, along with vegetables. You can take photos in the surrounding gardens and farms and buy fresh produce.

blocks.title: Drive past the Del Monte pineapple plantation

children.text: The Camp Phillips area on the way up to Dahilayan is covered in pineapple fields stretching to the horizon. The view from the car alone gives a real sense of Bukidnon's scale.
Staying at a lodge means the temperature drops sharply after sunset, making a campfire welcome. With little light pollution, clear nights bring out a sky full of stars.
Depart from Cagayan de Oro by car, passing the Camp Phillips pineapple fields, and arrive in Dahilayan.
Enjoy the
zipline, mountain coaster, and drop zone at the adventure park in turn. Mornings are clear and lines are shorter.
Have a hot lunch of soup dishes at a restaurant inside the park or a nearby lodge.
Enjoy the luge and rides at Dahilayan Forest Park, or walk through the pine forest.
Stop by the flower garden and a produce shop before heading back to Cagayan de Oro.
Check in at your lodge, walk through the pine forest, and enjoy a campfire and stargazing in the evening.
Take photos of the misty forest early in the morning, ride the zipline as soon as it opens, and head down around midday.
A direct flight from Manila to Laguindingan Airport (CGY) takes about
1 hour 25 minutes
, and about
50 minutes
from Cebu. From the airport to Dahilayan takes about
2 hours 30 minutes–3 hours
by car. Most travelers go via Cagayan de Oro's downtown; going straight from the airport is easiest with a chartered van (about
From the Agora bus terminal in Cagayan de Oro, take a bus or van bound for Malaybalay in Bukidnon and get off at Tankulan or Alae junction in Manolo Fortich (about
1 hour
, about
). From there, transfer to a jeepney or habal-habal (motorbike taxi) bound for Dahilayan, another
40 minutes–1 hour
up, at a fare of about
. Public transport connections are infrequent, so there may be no ride back late in the afternoon.
The most comfortable option is chartering a vehicle for the day from Cagayan de Oro, at about
a day including driver, letting you freely stop at Del Monte plantation and the flower garden. From Davao, it takes about
6–7 hours
along the Bukidnon highway.
Being on a plateau, Dahilayan runs 5–10 degrees cooler than the lowlands year-round, with midday temperatures generally 18–24 degrees and dawn temperatures dropping to 10–15 degrees. From
December
to
February
is the coolest stretch, good for enjoying a "highland winter," while from
March
to
May
, clearer skies make it the best time for the zipline and mountain views.
From
June
to
November

, afternoon rain and fog are frequent. The zipline and outdoor facilities pause operation during lightning or strong wind, so it's best to visit early in the morning during the wet season. On weekends around Christmas, New Year, Holy Week, and summer vacation (April–
May
), family crowds can push zipline waits past
1 hour
. Bukidnon's provincial Kaamulan Festival is held in late
February
to early March in Malaybalay, so visiting then lets you also catch performances of indigenous tribal culture.
Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions. Check the official page for the latest facility prices and operating status.
Within Dahilayan there are lodges run by the adventure park and forest park, pine-forest cabins, and small mountain lodges. These run about

a night, and bookings fill up early on weekends and holidays, so reserve ahead. Most places have no heating but provide thick blankets, so if you feel the cold, bring a thin padded jacket or fleece. For a day trip, a hotel in downtown Cagayan de Oro offers wider and cheaper options.

Warm food is a highland specialty here. Bulalo (beef bone marrow soup), tinola (chicken and ginger soup), and hot coffee or chocolate all pair well with the cool weather. Bukidnon is one of the Philippines' leading corn, pineapple, and vegetable regions, so roadside stalls sell cheap boiled corn, steamed corn cake (binaki), and fresh pineapple. Restaurants near the Del Monte plantation also serve steaks and grilled dishes with pineapple on the side.
The adventure park usually opens around
8 a.m.
. Arriving right at opening lets you ride the zipline with no wait, and the weather is clearest then too.
The zipline and drop zone have weight limits (roughly 30–40 kg minimum, 100–120 kg maximum) and age restrictions. If you're traveling with children, check the conditions on-site first.
Wear sneakers instead of sandals, and leave your belongings in a locker. A neck-strap waterproof phone pouch or an action-camera mount lets you safely capture video.
It's windy even at midday and rain is frequent in the afternoon. Bring a thin windbreaker and long pants.
The village has no ATM, and small shops take cash only. It's safer to withdraw the cash you need in Cagayan de Oro beforehand.
If you took public transport, be sure to confirm the last jeepney back. After
4 p.m.
, rides can be hard to find.
Photos are at their best before
9 a.m.
, when sunlight filters through the pines, or in the afternoon when fog settles in.
The zipline stops immediately if there's lightning or strong wind. Follow the safety staff's judgment, and don't stay near metal structures while waiting for it to resume.
Highland roads are steep and slippery when wet. Ask for a helmet when riding a habal-habal, and avoid driving in the evening when fog is thick.
Avoid the zipline and drop zone if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, a back or neck injury, or are pregnant.
The Kitanglad mountain range is a protected area. It's best not to go deep into the forest without a guide or stray off the trails.
Some remote mountainous parts of Bukidnon have reported security concerns. Stick to tourist areas and main roads, and check your home country's latest travel advisory before you go.
Before using the zipline, double-check your harness and safety line fastening with a staff member. Ask right away for a replacement if the gear doesn't fit properly.
